meta.title: Syzygeon – Planetary alignments
meta.description: The tightest groupings of the planets between 13,200 BC and AD 17,191, computed with the JPL DE441 ephemeris.
title: Syzygeon
lede.generic: The tightest groupings of the planets, computed with the JPL DE441 ephemeris.
lede.range: The tightest groupings of the planets from {from} to {to}, computed with the JPL DE441 ephemeris.
repo.title: View the source code of Syzygeon on GitHub
kind.axis: Along a line through the Sun
kind.side: All on one side of the Sun
measure.hint3d: The amplitude is the largest distance between any two bodies, latitude included.
hint.moonHelio: Seen from the Sun the Moon is never more than 0.15° from the Earth, so it barely changes the results.
hint.sunHelio: Seen from the Sun, the Sun is the point of view, so it cannot be part of the group.
hint.outliers: Leaving bodies out is offered while at least {n} planets stay in the group.
results.yearsHint: Years are astronomical: 0 is 1 BC, −3101 is 3102 BC.
results.elong: At least this far from the Sun, degrees
eclipseFilter.any: Only with an eclipse within ±2 days
coverage.full: Dataset covers the whole range. Exported {date}.
coverage.partial: Dataset covers {pct} % of the range so far. Exported {date}.

caption.centredSun: Seen from above, centred on the Sun.
caption.centredEarth: Seen from above, centred on the Earth.
caption.even: Orbits evenly spaced; directions are exact.
caption.sqrt: Distances on a square-root scale; directions are exact.
caption.switchSun: Switch the centre to the Sun to see the shaded region of this criterion.
caption.switchEarth: Switch the centre to the Earth to see the shaded region of this criterion.
caption.axis: The shaded band is the narrowest one through the Sun holding the group.
caption.geo: The shaded sector is the arc of sky the group spans in longitude.
caption.side: The shaded sector is the smallest one, seen from the Sun, holding the group.
caption.dimmed: Dimmed bodies are not part of the group.
results.label: Results
timeline.titleAmp: Amplitude of every stored grouping, {from} to {to}
timeline.titleSep: Largest separation of every stored grouping, {from} to {to}
timeline.aria: Amplitude of every stored grouping over time; tighter groupings are higher
timeline.hint: Higher means tighter. Click a dot to see that date; drag across the chart to zoom into those years, double-click to zoom back out.

summary.dates.one: {n} date, oldest first. The tightest one is highlighted.
summary.dates.other: {n} dates, oldest first. The tightest one is highlighted.

summary.none: Nothing matches these settings. Widen the amplitude, the years or the other filters.
summary.truncated: Only the first {n} are listed; the CSV has them all.
summary.cap: The dataset only holds groupings up to {cap} for this criterion.
summary.notAvailable: This combination is not in the dataset.
summary.loadError: The data for this criterion could not be loaded: {error}.
summary.noDataset: No dataset found: {error}. Run export_web.py and publish the docs/data folder next to this page.
details.afterPrevious: {days} days after the previous one in the list.
details.hidden: Not in the list: a better grouping nearby hides it.
stel.hint: The date and the Julian Day open this moment in Stellarium Web, seen from a place where the group is overhead. Press {key} there to switch the atmosphere off and see the planets in daylight.
stel.far: This far from the present its simpler planetary theory may place the planets differently from DE441.
stel.title: Open this moment in Stellarium Web
sent.geo: Seen from the Earth, {subject} fit in {amp} of sky.
sent.axis: {Subject} lie in a band {amp} wide around a line through the Sun.
sent.side: Seen from the Sun, {subject} fit in a sector of {amp}.
sent.3d: No two of them are more than {amp} apart in the sky, latitude included.
sent.elong: Every body of the group is at least {deg} from the Sun.
note.plane: Longitudes are measured in the invariable plane of the solar system, from its node on the celestial equator, not from the equinox.
note.ecliptic: Longitudes are ecliptic longitudes of J2000.
note.tropical: Seen from the Earth, on the ecliptic and from the mean equinox of the date (tropical zodiac).
note.sidereal: Seen from the Earth, on the ecliptic of the date, measured from the Lahiri sidereal origin (ayanamsha {ayan}).
note.greyed: Greyed rows are not part of the group.
footer.text: Positions from JPL DE441 (Park et al. 2021), {plane}. Tropical longitudes use the long-term precession of Vondrák et al. (2011); sidereal ones the Lahiri ayanamsha. ΔT from Morrison & Stephenson (2004) as given by Espenak & Meeus, with uncertainties after Huber (2000). Computed with {code}.
footer.planeInvariable: projected onto the invariable plane of the solar system
